== Spring Quality ==
* Alkaline {{ill|Simple Hot Springs|ja|単純温泉}}, source temperature 84°C

== Hot Spring Town ==
[[File:Gero-onsen01s3200.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Hot spring town and {{ill|Mount Nakane|ja|中根山|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11366225}} (Gero Fuji)]]

Lodging facilities such as {{ill|Ryokan|en|Ryokan|qid=Q562930|lt=ryokan}} and {{ill|Hotel|en|Hotel|qid=Q27686|lt=hotels}} line the banks along the {{ill|Hida River|en|Hida River|qid=Q3366160|lt=Hida River}} (also known as the {{ill|Masuda River|ja|益田川|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11581254}}), centered around {{ill|Gero Station|en|Gero Station|qid=Q873111|lt=Gero Station}}. In addition to along the river, accommodations are found on the slopes of the hills on both banks – many of which offer shuttle bus service to {{ill|Gero Station|en|Gero Station|qid=Q873111|lt=Gero Station}}.<ref>例：{{Cite web|url=http://www.yunoshimakan.co.jp/access/|title=Yunoshimakan – Transportation and Sightseeing|publisher={{ill|Yunoshimakan|ja|湯之島館}}|date=2018-09-28|accessdate=2019-10-13|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20180928111323/http://www.yunoshimakan.co.jp/access/|archivedate=2018-09-28}}</ref> Note: In the town names of {{ill|Gero, Gifu|ar|غيرو (غيفو)|az|Qero|azb|قرو، قیفو|ce|Геро|ceb|Gero-shi|de|Gero (Gifu)|es|Gero|fa|گرو، گیفو|fi|Gero (Gifu)|fr|Gero (Gifu)|gl|Gero|it|Gero (Giappone)|ja|下呂市|ko|게로시|mg|Gero|my|ဂဲရိုမြို့၊ ဂိဖု|mzn|گرو، گیفو|nl|Gero (Gifu)|pl|Gero (miasto)|pt|Gero (Gifu)|ro|Gero (localitate)|ru|Геро|su|Gero, Gifu|sv|Gero, Gifu|tg|Геро|th|เกโระ|tl|Gero, Gifu|tr|Gero|tt|Геро|uk|Ґеро (Ґіфу)|ur|گیرو، گیفو|vi|Gero, Gifu|war|Gero, Gifu|zh|下呂市|zh_classical|下呂市|zh_min_nan|Gero-chhī|zh_yue|下呂|qid=Q819639|lt=Gero City}}, the western side of the river is known as {{ill|Koda|en|Koda|qid=Q1223964|lt=Kōden}} (which includes {{ill|Gero Station|en|Gero Station|qid=Q873111|lt=Gero Station}}), while on the eastern side the area north of the road beyond {{ill|Gero Ōhashi|ja|下呂大橋}} (along Adano-dōri) is called {{ill|Yunoshima|ja|湯之島}}, and the southern side is known as Mori. Most of the accommodations fall within these three districts, although the far northwestern lodging is located in the former {{ill|Hagiwara-chō|ja|萩原町|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11620353}} area of {{ill|Mashita District, Gifu|en|Mashita District, Gifu|qid=Q6783168|lt=Masuda District}} (currently {{ill|Hagiwara-cho, Gero City|ja|下呂市萩原町西上田}}).

== Hotels and Ryokan ==
There is a wide range of lodging available – from traditional ryokan and luxury hotels to business hotels. For details, please refer to the website of the [http://www.gero-spa.or.jp/]. Note that some accommodations are not affiliated with the cooperative (for example, {{ill|Ōedo Onsen Monogatari Gero Shinkan|ja|大江戸温泉物語 下呂新館}}).

The Gero Onsen Ryokan Cooperative also issues a "Yumeguri Tegata" (Hot Spring Tour Voucher). Although the vouchers have an expiration date, each voucher allows the holder to visit and bathe at any three participating establishments.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.gero-spa.or.jp/yu_meguri/|title=Yumeguri Tegata|publisher={{ill|Gero Onsen Ryokan Cooperative|ja|下呂温泉旅館協同組合|qid=Q140447351}}|date=2019-08-14|accessdate=2019-10-13|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20190814104626/http://www.gero-spa.or.jp/yu_meguri/|archivedate=2019-08-14}}</ref>

== Public Baths ==
There are three public baths ({{ill|soto-yu|ja|外湯}} ({{ill|Public bathing|en|Public bathing|qid=Q785952|lt=Public Bathhouse}})): Kua Garden Open-Air Bath, {{ill|Shirasagi no Yu|ja|白鷺の湯}}, and {{ill|Kōno Yu|ja|幸乃湯}}.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.city.gero.lg.jp/kankou/node_7779/node_29737/node_37101/node_37104|title=Day-Use Bath Facilities in the Gero Onsen Town|publisher={{ill|Gero City Tourism Division|ja|下呂市役所 観光商工部 観光課}}|date=2019-03-20|accessdate=2019-10-13|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20190402011550/http://www.city.gero.lg.jp/kankou/node_7779/node_29737/node_37101/node_37104|archivedate=2019-04-02}}</ref>

== Climate ==
The climate of Gero Onsen is a mountain inland climate, being surrounded by mountains. There is a significant temperature variation throughout the day, so in spring and autumn a jacket that can be easily put on or taken off is recommended.<ref>[https://www.hankyu-travel.com/onsen/gero/hotspring.php]{{ill|Gero Onsen Tidbits|ja|下呂温泉豆知識}} (Hankyu Travel, viewed February 26, 2020)</ref>

In the Hida region, particularly in the southern parts and on the Pacific side of the water system, snowfall occurs but is not excessive.<ref>[https://ja.weatherspark.com/y/143604/下呂市、日本における年間の平均的な気候　下呂市 Weatherspark, viewed February 26, 2020]</ref>

== History ==
The origin of the hot spring dates back to between the Enki and Tenryaku periods of the 10th century, when a hot spring began erupting near the summit of Yukagamamine (1,067 m) located to the east of the current hot spring area. It was reputed to have healing properties, attracting therapeutic bathers from the very beginning.<ref name=gero>[{{NDLDC|1057310/14}}　下呂温泉]『湯の街下呂』 (Gero Town, 1933)</ref>

In 1265 (Bun'ei 2), the eruption from the mountain summit ceased, but a new spring was discovered on the riverbed of the {{ill|Hida River|en|Hida River|qid=Q3366160|lt=Hida River}}, which is the present hot spring area. This discovery is preserved in the {{ill|Hot Spring Discovery Legend|ja|開湯伝説}}, specifically the "White Egret Legend" in which {{ill|Bhaisajyaguru|en|Bhaisajyaguru|qid=Q854773|lt=Yakushi Nyorai Medicine Buddha}} transformed into a white egret to signal the location of the spring. With the shifting of the spring’s outlet, the statue of Yakushi Nyorai that had been enshrined at Yukagamamine was relocated to the village, establishing the {{ill|Onsen Temple|ja|温泉寺|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11562939}}.<ref name=gero/>

During the Muromachi period, the {{ill|Kyoto Gozan|ja|五山僧|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 京都五山|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q8193432}} and {{ill|Banrishūku|ja|万里集九|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11353943}} introduced Gero Onsen nationwide as one of the "Three Famous Hot Springs" along with {{ill|Kusatsu Onsen|en|Kusatsu Onsen|qid=Q3137477|lt=Kusatsu Onsen}} and {{ill|Arima Onsen|en|Arima Onsen|qid=Q4790673|lt=Arima Onsen}}<ref name=onsen>[http://www.onsenji.jp/history/index.html?admin=view　History of Onsen-dera] Gero Onsen, Iorui Reizan, Onsen-dera</ref>. In 1621, {{ill|Hayashi Razan|en|Hayashi Razan|qid=Q558279|lt=Hayashirasan}} also cited it as a famed hot spring in his writings. The Onsen-dera, built at the foot of {{ill|Mount Nakane|ja|中根山|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11366225}}, is said to have been founded in the Edo period (1671)<ref name=onsen/>. At that time the spring was called “Yushima,” and later, Yunoshima Onsen became used as an alternate name for Gero Onsen.<ref name=gero/>. Although the hot spring area has repeatedly suffered catastrophic damage from flooding of the {{ill|Hida River|en|Hida River|qid=Q3366160|lt=Hida River}}, it was always rebuilt; however, during the great flood of the {{ill|Ansei|en|Ansei|qid=Q1327259|lt=Ansei}} era, the hot spring vein was destroyed and the outlet lost, leading to a period of decline in the Meiji era.<ref name=gero/>

In an effort to revive the spring, local residents began boring excavation during the {{ill|Taishō era|ja|大正時代|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 大正|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q329174}}<ref name=gero/>, and in the early Shōwa period, anticipating the opening of the {{ill|Takayama Main Line|de|Takayama-Hauptlinie|et|Takayama põhiliin|fr|Ligne principale Takayama|it|Linea principale Takayama|ja|高山本線|ko|다카야마 본선|su|Jalur Utama Takayama|zh|高山本線|qid=Q1188357|lt=Takayama Main Line}} at {{ill|Gero Station|en|Gero Station|qid=Q873111|lt=Gero Station}} in 1930 (Shōwa 5), Nagoya businessman Takehachi Iwata – the founder of {{ill|Madras|ja|マドラス (企業)|lt=Madras|lt_ja=マドラス|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11340682}} – embarked on a mining venture and opened Yunoshima-kan in 1931 (Shōwa 6).<ref>[http://www.niwa-ae.com/ourworks/old_yunoshima.htm Yunoshima-kan] (Niwa Eiji Architectural Office)</ref> The building of this ryokan has since been designated as a Registered Tangible Cultural Property of Japan.<ref>[http://www.yunoshimakan.co.jp/about/history.html History of Yunoshima-kan] (Yunoshima-kan, viewed February 20, 2020)</ref>.

== Origin of the Place Name ==
The name “Gero” dates back to the Ritsuryō system. According to the {{ill|Shoku Nihongi|en|Shoku Nihongi|qid=Q611399|lt=Shoku Nihongi}}, in 776 AD (Hōki 2), near Gero Onsen there existed stations – one, {{ill|Sugata Station|ja|菅田駅}}, in {{ill|Mino Province|en|Mino Province|qid=Q864156|lt=Mino Province}}, and another, Ban'yū (Uwedome Station), in {{ill|Hida Province|en|Hida Province|qid=Q1056535|lt=Hida Province}} ({{ill|Ōno District, Gifu|en|Ōno District, Gifu|qid=Q31671|lt=Ōno District}}).<ref>[http://www.city.gero.lg.jp/kankou/view.rbz?of=1&ik=0&pnp=14&cd=26 Gero City Tourism Information]</ref> However, because the two stations were far apart and the roads were steep, a new station, Shimonodome Station, was established midway. Over time, the pronunciation evolved from “Shimonodome” to “Gero.” 

Sugata Station was located in what is now {{ill|Sugata, Kanayama-cho, Gero City|ja|下呂市金山町菅田}}, and Ban'yū Station was in {{ill|Hagiwara-cho, Gero City|ja|下呂市萩原町上呂}}.

== Landmarks ==
=== Fountain Pool ===
[[File:Gero Spa Kawararoten.JPG|thumb|right|250px|Hot Spring Fountain Area (Open-Air Bath on the Riverbed)]]

At Gero Onsen, a hot spring facility known as the "Fountain Pool" was established in 1983 (Shōwa 58) along the riverbed of the {{ill|Hida River|en|Hida River|qid=Q3366160|lt=Hida River}} so that visitors can bathe casually.<ref name="yomiuri20211128">{{Cite web|url=https://www.yomiuri.co.jp/national/20211128-OYT1T50159/|title=Customers Not Observing Bathing Etiquette Cause Trouble, Leading to Complaints – Famous Hot Spring Now “Foot Bath Only”|accessdate=2021-12-01|website={{ill|The Yomiuri Shimbun|en|Yomiuri Shimbun|qid=Q645218|lt=Yomiuri Shimbun}}}}</ref> Although the Fountain Pool, as a free open-air bath, has repeatedly been submerged by heavy rains and received sediment deposits, it has continued in operation with adjustments to its location and scale.<ref name="yomiuri20211128" /> From February 1, 2010 (Heisei 22), both men and women were required to wear swimsuits when using it<ref>[http://www.gero-spa.com/spot/detail/2 Guidelines on Swimsuit Use at the Fountain Pool – Gero Onsen Tourism Association]</ref><ref>[http://www.city.gero.lg.jp/kankou/view.rbz?nd=101&ik=1&pnp=100&pnp=101&cd=26 Information on the Fountain Pool – Gero City Tourism Division]</ref> However, due to complaints over rule violations and concerns for the surrounding scenery, its operation has been revised.<ref name="yomiuri20211128" /> From December 1, 2021 (Reiwa 3), the Fountain Pool has been designated exclusively as a foot bath.<ref name="yomiuri20211128" /><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.asahi.com/articles/DA3S15128546.html|title=Gero Onsen Symbol Now Dedicated to Foot Baths – Riverbed, Without Enforcing Swimsuit Rules: Asahi Shimbun Digital|newspaper=|date=2021-11-30}}</ref>
* Location (Hot Spring Fountain Area): {{ウィキ座標度分秒|35|48|27.2|N|137|14|27.4|E|scale:20000}}

=== Foot Baths ===
Numerous foot baths are installed throughout Gero Onsen.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.gero-spa.or.jp/ashiyu/|title=Foot Bath Guide|publisher={{ill|Gero Onsen Ryokan Cooperative|ja|下呂温泉旅館協同組合|qid=Q140447351}}|date=2018-09-03|accessdate=2019-10-13|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20180903005904/http://www.gero-spa.or.jp/ashiyu/|archivedate=2018-09-03}}</ref> The very first, known as “Sagi no Ashiyu” (Heron Foot Bath), was established in 2000 (Heisei 12).<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.gero-spa.com/shukuhaku/|title=New Attraction in Gero: "Sagi no Ashiyu"|publisher={{ill|Gero Onsen Ryokan Cooperative|ja|下呂温泉旅館協同組合|qid=Q140447351}}|date=2000-07-05|accessdate=2019-10-13|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20191013132437/http://www.gero-spa.or.jp/blog/page/44|archivedate=2019-10-13}}</ref>

=== Fire-Fishing ===
Fire-Fishing is a traditional method that exploits the natural behavior of {{ill|Ayu sweetfish|ja|鮎|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to アユ|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q642906}} (sweetfish) – which, when descending the river to spawn, are driven by setting nets and using bonfires and torches to force them into the nets. This technique is practiced on the {{ill|Maze River (Japan)|en|Maze River (Japan)|qid=Q258070|lt=Masase River}} annually from late August to late September.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.gero-spa.com/spot/detail.php?id=132|title=Fire-Fishing on the Masase River|access-date=2022-10-25|publisher={{ill|Gero Onsen Tourism Association|ja|下呂温泉観光協会}}}}</ref>

== Souvenirs ==
* Okudaya Gero Ointment – A locally produced medicated plaster made with a blend of ingredients including {{ill|Ou-baku|ja|黄蘗}} (also known as Kihada) and {{ill|Myrica rubra|ja|楊梅皮|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to ヤマモモ|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q311617}} (Yōbaibi), manufactured by {{ill|Okudaya Matayemon Kōhonpo|ja|奥田又右衛門膏本舗|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11445999}}.
* {{ill|hōba miso|ja|朴葉味噌|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11521610}} – Miso wrapped in cypress (kōya) leaves; some varieties include ground {{ill|Hida Beef|ja|飛騨牛|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11665910}}.
* Tochi-no-mi Senbei – Rice crackers made with {{ill|Aesculus turbinata|ja|栃の実|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to トチノキ|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q1132580}}, known for their sweetness and soft texture.<ref>{{Cite book|和書|title=Okashi Fūdoki|date=1965th year 8月15日|year=1965|publisher={{ill|Hayakawa Publishing|en|Hayakawa Publishing|qid=Q11511323|lt=Hayakawa Shobō}}|pages=110-111}}</ref>
* {{ill|Sarubobo|en|Sarubobo|qid=Q1697067|lt=Sarubobo}} – Literally “baby monkey,” a faceless doll dressed in red.
* Pickled Items – A variety of pickles made from local Hida specialties such as “aka kabura” (red turnips) are widely available in souvenir shops and local supermarkets.
